key_insight: This paper shows that neural decoders can benefit from large amounts of unlabelled spike data, not just labelled sessions, by pretraining a model that learns general neural patterns before decoding behavior. The result is a more robust decoder that transfers better across sessions and likely improves performance when labels are scarce.
problem_solved: Current spike-based neural decoding models usually require paired neural activity and behavioural labels, which limits training to small supervised datasets. This paper tackles the lack of scalable pretraining for neural population decoding on unlabelled data.
method: Introduce MOJO, a masked autoencoder-style framework for neural spike data.
Pretrain on unlabelled neural recordings by masking parts of the spike sequence and learning to reconstruct them.
Transfer the pretrained representations to downstream decoding tasks, improving generalization across sessions and subjects.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners working in neurotechnology, this offers a path to build stronger decoders with less reliance on expensive labelled data. It also aligns neural decoding with modern self-supervised learning, opening the door to larger-scale and more generalizable models.

paper_title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
paper_authors: Ximeng Mao, Nanda H. Krishna, Avery Hee-Woon Ryoo, Matthew G. Perich, Guillaume Lajoie
